column3: And after we had been brought safely through, we learned that the island was called Malta.
The local people showed us extraordinary kindness, for because of the rain that had begun and because of the cold, they kindled a fire and welcomed us all.
But when Paul gathered a bundle of sticks and put them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened onto his hand.

When the local people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they began saying to one another, “Certainly this man is a murderer, whom Justice did not allow to live even though he was saved from the sea.”
But he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.
They were expecting him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after waiting a long time and observing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and began saying that he was a god.
Now in the areas around that place were lands belonging to the leading man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
And it happened that the father of Publius was lying sick with fever and dysentery. Paul went in to him, prayed, laid his hands on him, and healed him.
After this happened, the rest of those on the island who had sicknesses also came and were being healed.
They also honored us with many honors, and when we were about to sail, they put on board the things we needed.
After three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island, whose emblem was the Twin Gods.
And after landing at Syracuse, we stayed three days.
From there we went around and came to Rhegium. And after one day a south wind arose, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
where we found brothers and were urged to stay with them seven days. And in this way we came to Rome.
And from there the brothers, hearing the things concerning us, came to meet us as far as the Market of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
And when we entered Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.

Now after three days he called together those who were leading men of the Jews. When they came together, he said to them, “Men and brothers, although I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, I was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
After examining me, they wanted to release me because there was no cause of death in me.
But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar—not as though I had anything to accuse my nation of.
For this reason, therefore, I called for you, to see and speak with you, for because of the hope of Israel I am wearing this chain.”
They said to him, “We neither received letters about you from Judea, nor has any of the brothers who came reported or spoken anything evil about you.
But we consider it right to hear from you what you think, for concerning this sect it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

And after arranging a day with him, even more people came to him at his lodging, to whom he explained, solemnly testifying about the kingdom of God and trying to persuade them about Jesus from both the law of Moses and the prophets, from morning until evening.
And some were being persuaded by the things spoken, but others were disbelieving.
And disagreeing with one another, they began leaving after Paul said one word: “The Holy Spirit spoke well through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,
saying, ‘Go to this people and say: Hearing you will hear and certainly not understand, and seeing you will see and certainly not perceive.

For the heart of this people has become dull, and with their ears they barely heard, and they closed their eyes, lest they should ever see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I will heal them.’
Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they also will listen.”
And he remained a whole two years in his own rented lodging and welcomed all who came to him,
proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, unhindered.
